definitions.explanation: How well a blade or cutting tool cuts. The quality or degree of sharpness.
The sharpness or effectiveness of words, arguments, or actions. Used figuratively for things that are sharp and decisive.

examples.japanese: この{包丁|ほうちょう}は{切|き}れ{味|あじ}がいい。
examples.english: This kitchen knife has good sharpness.

examples.japanese: {切|き}れ{味|あじ}が{落|お}ちたナイフを{研|と}いだ。
examples.english: I sharpened the knife that had lost its edge.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しいはさみは{切|き}れ{味|あじ}が{抜群|ばつぐん}だ。
examples.english: The new scissors have outstanding sharpness.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}の{発言|はつげん}は{切|き}れ{味|あじ}が{鋭|するど}い。
examples.english: Her remarks are sharp and incisive.

examples.japanese: {今日|きょう}のプレゼンは{切|き}れ{味|あじ}のある{内容|ないよう}だった。
examples.english: Today's presentation had sharp, incisive content.

examples.japanese: {年齢|ねんれい}を{重|かさ}ねても、{彼|かれ}の{批評|ひひょう}の{切|き}れ{味|あじ}は{衰|おとろ}えない。
examples.english: Even as he ages, the sharpness of his criticism doesn't decline.

notes: Common collocations: {切|き}れ{味|あじ}がいい/わるい (good/bad sharpness), {切|き}れ{味|あじ}が{鋭|するど}い (sharp), {切|き}れ{味|あじ}が{落|お}ちる (to lose its edge), {切|き}れ{味|あじ}が{抜群|ばつぐん} (outstanding sharpness). The figurative sense is widely used for speeches, writing, wit, and athletic moves.
